cards.title: pcVPC Principle and Normalization
cards.claim: Prediction-corrected VPCs (pcVPC) remove variability arising from differences in independent variables (e.g., dose, covariates) within a bin by normalizing the dependent variable (observed and simulated) based on the typical population prediction for the median independent variable in that bin.
conditions: Applicable when traditional VPCs are hampered by binning across large variability in dose or influential covariates.
Requires a mixed-effects model capable of generating typical population predictions (PRED).
For log-transformed dependent variables, the transformation must be adjusted to allow correct prediction correction.
required_inputs: Fitted mixed-effects model (fixed and random effects).
Observed data with independent variables (time, dose, covariates).
Typical population predictions (PRED) for each observation.
Median typical population prediction for each bin of independent variables.
limitations: Prediction correction transforms the y-axis scale, making it less intuitive than raw concentration units.

Censored data (e.g., BQL) cannot be directly handled by standard pcVPC rank-based methods; they must be omitted from both observed and simulated datasets before calculating statistics, requiring accurate prediction of censoring frequency.
Does not replace the need for other diagnostics; it is one tool in a toolbox.
cards.downstream_use: Model qualification and diagnostic evaluation of population PK/PD models, specifically for assessing random effects structure and structural model misspecification in the presence of covariate or dose variability.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
